reviews.t: Worth figuring out how to lather
reviews.x: Before I purchased this I had heard that it was hard to lather. I read shaving forums that said to use warm water not hot, to load lots of soap on the brush and to face lather instead of using a bowl. I did all these things and got terrible lather. So I did just the opposite. Hot water, regular amount on my brush and I lathered using a bowl and now it works extremely well. Super thick lather. It went from being my least favorite to being one of my absolute favorites. If you have bought some and

There are shaving creams and shaving soaps ... and then, there's Mitchell's Wool Fat!  Seriously ... if you're shaving with a double edge razor and not shaving with this, you have no idea what you're missing.  Lubrication is unmatched. And lather? Well ... get a good badger hair brush (Perfector makes a nice one), watch the youtube video on how to lather Wool Fat - and you'll have no trouble building up a thick layer of lather FAST! Some say this soap is hard to lather, but first time using it I had no problems making more than enough lather. It cushions great, and helps give a close non-irritating shave. If I had one complaint it would be the scent. Just overly soap-like to me. I know, it is a soap, but wow, the scent just seems so...cleaning product like. Almost wish it had no smell at all. I prefer scents like sandalwood or bay rum. Still, it is a great soap that I will use again.

After hearing many times of "the fat" I decided to buy my own puck of Mitchell's and see what the fuss was about. It turned out to be a really great soap though not my favorite.  Lather: Doesn't bloom into a full lather avalanche like TOBS does for me but isn't too thin either. Certainly adequate.  Face Protection: On the slick side, good blade glide. It's ok, but doesn't obviously stand out above less expensive soaps I've used. I don't mind spending more for a superior product, but I find this soap to be average.

As YMMV when taking someone's word on shave gear, I thought I might provide some background about me:  I have gentle to oily skin and stiff, tough neck hairs.  I used to think I had sensitive skin until I married someone with actual sensitive skin. I've tried at least a dozen shave soaps, maybe two dozen.  MWF is my go-to, standard. I leave it in a shave bowl in a drawer.  I rinse my brush and then swirl the dripping wet brush on top of the soap.  In about 20 seconds, you have phenomenal lather.  Wet and repeat for more water if needed. Lather around your face further as needed.  I often do this, then take a shower and repeat the lathering when I get out of the shower, and then shave. reviews.t: Once thought this was the best shaving soap I have ever used; not so sure now
reviews.x: I have been shaving with a brush and a mug for nearly 50 years.  This is, without a question, the best shaving soap I have ever used (and I have used many different brands, cheap and expensive).  The wool lanolin in this soap seems to be the key ingredient.  The lather on my face stays wetter longer than any other shaving soap I have used.  The result is a smooth, comfortable shave even after several days of beard growth.  My only complaint is the scent, which is a bit too musky for my taste --

reviews.t: Tough to lather if your water is hard
reviews.x: For me the real test of a shaving soap is if it provides enough cushion to allow me to get a close shave 5 mornings in a row without irritation.  By that standard, this soap is among the very best out there.  But one word of warning.  Mitchell's Wool Fat Shaving Soap does not lather well in hard (high mineral content) water. So if your water comes from a well, you may as well not use it. You'll never get much out of it no matter how hot your water is.  Otherwise, for me this soap is among the be

reviews.t: As a new shaver, this is amazing.
reviews.x: Bought this at the recommendation of many online forums for it's newb-friendly lather, and will probably stick with it for a long time to come. Lathers even with hard water, smells like an old barber shop (not to strong, just a nice light fragrance you would expect from shaving creams). This is a Face-Lathering soap, and you may need to soak it in warm, but not hot, water while you soak your brush for the best results. Thoroughly impressed. Very Nice Lather. If shaving is more to you than just something you have to do, this soap will please.

Mitchell's wool fat shaving soaps have been around for a long time, and it's easy to see why. This review is based on results using a safety razor. Soaking the puck for 10 minutes prior to shaving, then loading the brush upside down and face lathering seems to work the best with this soap. Lathering correctly with MWF soap causes the blade to effortlessly glide across the face, minimizing irritation. This also leaves the face feeling soft and healthy after the shave. Great lather and shave, but I learned I'm allergic to lanolin and I got a horrible rash. So if you're not allergic, a great shave and really softens the hair.

But that doesn't stop me from making a really nice lather with this. I prefer to use a boar brush with soaps but badger works well too. I know the water is very soft here and it's also in the tropics so most of the time the ambient temperature is close to body temperature which may help. claims.text: Reviewers widely praise the thick, slick lather and smooth, comfortable shaves it provides.
Many note the soap leaves skin feeling great and reduces irritation, including less alum burn.
Several reviewers mention it takes extra time, water, or technique to lather properly, though most find it worth it.
A few reviewers find the scent overly plain or soap-like.
A minority consider it average or not worth the higher price compared to cheaper soaps.
